facts.text: The token evaluation was measured on 2026-11-09 on the seeded subject Memos/Home with 24 live facts, estimating tokens as characters divided by four for text and pixels divided by 750 for images.
Arm C, the primary sources (4 git files plus 3 declared screenshots), costs 17171 tokens.
Arm A, the raw search JSON of the 24 facts, costs 1476 tokens.
Arm A2, the same facts as bare text lines, costs 371 tokens.
Arm B, the compiled dossier at budget 1200, full depth, markdown, costs 708 tokens.
The compiled dossier is about 24 times smaller than the primary sources (B/C 0.04), about half the raw JSON (B/A 0.48), and 1.91 times the bare fact lines.
Two independent agents, one given only arm A and one only arm B, each answered the ten evaluation questions 10 out of 10, including three contradiction questions and two unanswerable ones.
Limit: at 24 facts compile is a net token cost against bare fact lines, because citations cost tokens and every fact is relevant; capture carries the compression.
at: - At 24 facts, compile is a net token cost

facts.text: Limit: selection correctness at 1000 facts is unmeasured; the scaling table proves the cost is bounded, not that the right facts were chosen.
at: - Selection correctness at 1000 facts is unmeasured.

facts.text: The project's success bar, at least 90 percent of raw-dump accuracy at no more than 25 percent of the tokens across two evaluation domains, is not yet established: only one domain is measured.
At a strict budget of 1200 the dossier costs 892 tokens and emits 39 facts whether the subject holds 50, 200 or 1000 facts, while plain facts grow from 625 to 12500 tokens.
The fleet evaluation was measured on 2026-11-20 with four writer agents and one reader, each a real dossier mcp process on one database, with no model called.
Fleet result: 50 of 50 depth-4 derivation chains were reconstructed with the writer identity preserved at every hop.
Fleet result: 200 of 200 pairs of contradictory writes with near-identical prose were both admitted and surfaced as a conflict citing both facts.
Fleet result: after two writers wrote the same slot, 200 of 200 slots had exactly one live value and 0 of 200 superseded facts were returned by default search or compile.
at: | Supersession | exactly one live value per slot

facts.text: Fleet result: 100 of 100 corrections by another agent's supersedes ref took effect and 0 of 100 corrected facts were returned by default search or compile.
at: | Correction | another agent's `supersedes` ref takes effect

facts.text: Fleet result: 120 of 120 descendants of a changed input verified stale with the right input named, all three read surfaces agreed, and the same-claim control gave 0 of 30 false stales.
at: | Derivation currency | descendant of a changed input verifies stale

facts.text: Fleet result: 0 of 20 retracted facts, or their text, came back through search or compile, and all 20 kept a tombstone with id and writer.
at: | Revocation | retracted fact, or its text, returned by search or compile

facts.text: Fleet result: 20 of 20 writes were visible to another agent's cursor on its first poll.
at: | Propagation | write visible to another agent's cursor on its first poll

facts.text: Fleet result: when four agents posted one keyed fact at once, 20 of 20 times the store ended with one row and one id and nothing else journalled.
at: | Convergence | four agents post one keyed fact at once

facts.text: Fleet finding: when two agents write different values to the same slot the later write supersedes the earlier and the overwritten value is never surfaced as a conflict (0 of 200).
Limit: the fleet evaluation is a self-evaluation of mechanism; no agent decided anything, so a correct label is shown to be necessary, not sufficient.
at: - It is a self-evaluation of mechanism.

facts.text: On one Apple-silicon laptop with a local SQLite file, get_fact took 0.3 ms per hop at the median and a write was visible to another agent within about 0.3 ms.

facts.text: Consequence: because import only works into an empty database, the git path is one-way promotion of a published bundle, not a way to push approved changes back into the same live store.
fact.schema.json describes content_hash as sha256 over normalized text, the canonical JSON of data, and sorted refs of (kind, target, locator).
ops.schema.json lists four post verdicts: new, deduped, replaced and near_duplicate.
The code hashes each ref as rel, kind, target and locator, so the contract's description of content_hash, which lists only kind, target and locator, omits rel.
No code path sets a dossier's degraded marker or keeps a last good dossier: Degraded is declared and never assigned, so the compile half of the fail-open guarantee is not implemented.
The code never returns the post verdict near_duplicate: a post is only ever new, deduped or replaced, and near duplicates are an advisory list from check.
A compile request's follow field is accepted and ignored, and a dossier's linked list is always empty; following refs in compile is not built.
at: follow is accepted but not used until Gate B

facts.text: A post request's idempotency_key and redact fields are declared in the contract and on the request type, and nothing in the write path reads them.
The contract allows an origin in a fact's provenance, and the provenance stamp the code writes has only actor, actor type, channel and posting time.
at: internal sealed record ProvenanceStamp(string Actor, string ActorType, string Channel, string PostedAt);

facts.text: A subject's pin is in the contract and the schema, and a subject inserted by post always gets a NULL pin; no command sets one.
ref.schema.json says the effective chain confidence is the minimum over refs, and no read computes it: ranking uses the fact's own confidence.
at: Effective chain confidence = MIN over refs.

facts.text: A ref's freshness fields (rev, snapshot, verified_at, valid) are stored and published, and no read path acts on them; checking external refs is reverify, which is not built.
at: checking them is reverify, which is not built
